A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECHO benchmark. Their main texts, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GNN experiments on five ECHO tasks in Tables 1–2, supplemented by sensitivity analyses, readout ablations, attention visualizations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and additionally reports ECHO-Energy sensitivity plots and further GRIT comparisons.

M1.justification: The benchmark-generation procedures, graph features, prediction targets, standardized model backbones, and training objective remain unchanged. No new algorithm or model component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate sssp, eccentricity, and diameter across the same six synthetic topologies, plus ECHO-Charge and ECHO-Energy on molecular graphs. The added Energy analyses examine an existing task and dataset rather than expand task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: GRIT, already present in the main benchmark comparisons, is added to Figures 8–9 and runtime Table 21. Figure 3's reported comparison changes from A-DGN versus GCN to GPS versus GCN, although its image is identical. The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes stated early-stopping patience from 100 to 50 epochs, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Figure 9 introduces common five-bin diameter grouping, replacing individual-diameter synthetic results and different ECHO-Charge bins. Dataset splits, maximum epochs, and hyperparameter-search budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices G.1–G.2 in v2 explicitly show ECHO-Energy depth and diameter sensitivity, which v1 omitted while asserting similarity to ECHO-Charge. The diagnostic comparisons also incorporate GRIT, and Figure 13 replaces the attention examples. Readout-depth and topology analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four independently seeded training runs, report means and standard deviations, and retain the same runtime repetition counts. Additional result entries follow existing reporting practices; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test appears.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and 17–20 retain their predictive scores. Supplementary results add Energy and GRIT series, replace Figure 13's attention patterns and weights, and change Figure 9's Charge profile from largest-bin deterioration to decreasing error across the revised bins. Table 21 revises several runtimes; GPS's Charge training time changes from 513.908 to 788.985 seconds per epoch. These revisions do not establish same-setting accuracy gains.

T1.justification: Task definitions, graph-construction formulas, geometric-invariance statements, and the loss expression remain equivalent. Neither version contains a theoretical contribution that is added, removed, or substantively revised in the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same five-task benchmark, long-range propagation claims, chemical relevance, and assessment of current GNN limitations. The supplementary additions do not redefine the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the assertion that Energy behaves similarly to Charge with task-specific interpretations of depth variability and diameter sensitivity. It removes the claim that GCN and GIN deteriorate on larger Charge graphs and no longer presents Figure 3 as evidence specifically for non-dissipative architectures. No substantive new limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: The documented early-stopping hyperparameter changes from 100 to 50 epochs. The quantum-chemistry pipeline, software and hardware descriptions, hyperparameter-search tables, and code/data link are retained. The expanded reproducibility statement mainly directs readers to existing technical information.

R1.justification: v2 adds application references by Bacciu et al., Miglior et al., and Tolloso et al., and adds Hariri et al.'s ChebNet work and Trenta et al.'s SONAR to the LRGB discussion. The benchmark's positioning remains stable. Duplicate-reference removal and publication-metadata updates are editorial.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and prose edits, adds ethics and acknowledgments sections and an LLM-use appendix, and expands the reproducibility statement. Contact information and publication headers change, and appendix letters shift, while the main scientific narrative retains its organization.

P2.justification: Several key displays are substantially redesigned: Figure 1 becomes a larger colored two-row illustration; Figures 8–9 expand to five panels with revised axes and legends; and Figure 13 is redrawn. Table 21 gains GRIT rows and grouped dataset headers, while Figures 10–12 are regrouped onto one page. These changes materially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies explicit Energy sensitivity evidence where v1 offered only an assertion of similarity to Charge, and completes GRIT's diagnostic and runtime comparisons. Clearer topology illustrations also help readers inspect the benchmark. These are modest gains, with headline results unchanged. Unexplained revisions to early stopping, Charge curves, and the identical Figure 3's model attribution still limit auditability.
